newsitem.title: UK: Creator of Thomas the Tank Engine dies aged 85.
newsitem.headline: Creator of Thomas the Tank Engine dies aged 85.

text.p: Reverend Wilbert Awdry, the creator of the popular children's book character Thomas The Tank Engine, died at his home on Friday at the age of 85, friends said. He had been ill for several months.
Awdry invented Thomas in 1943 in a bid to entertain his son Christopher, who was sick in bed with measles.

His stories about the talkative steam trains and their carriages, each one with its own distinctive personality, were an immediate hit after his wife Margaret sent Awdry's outlines to a literary agent in 1945.
Generations of children were thrilled by the exploits of Thomas, James the Red Engine, Henry the Green Engine, Gordon the Blue Engine and the Fat Controller.
Awdry, who produced 26 books before handing over the reins to Christopher, always professed himself surprised at the runaway success of Thomas and his friends.
In all the father and son team wrote 40 books, which sold many millions of copies all over the world and spawned a vast amount of merchandise which was especially popular in Japan.
The trains also appeared in 104 televised episodes narrated by former Beatle drummer Ringo Star.
A spokesman for Britt Allcroft, the producer of the series, said another 26 episodes would be made this year. The company was floated on the London stock exchange last November to great success.
Awdry's interest in railways began as a child when he lived near a mainline track in the south of England and started inventing names and characters for the engines.

He maintained an obsessive interest in the stories, even when they were being written by Christopher, and refused to bow to modern critics who complained that the only female characters in the tales were a string of carriages.
Awdry was awarded an Order of the British Empire for his work in 1996. He was born on June 15, 1911 and is survived by three children.
